**Access to the SFN** , which had already been at high levels, expanded in 2020, with the inclusion of 14 million citizens in the system. With this, 96% of the adult population in Brazil established some kind of financial relationship. In addition to this most recent expansion of access, the past analysis showed that the **diversification of providers** has changed the landscape of institutions that provide financial services to the Brazilian citizen, especially the IPs, which were responsible for about 30% of the new relationships established in the analyzed period. 

Regarding **products and services** , in the last three years the population with some credit operation increased slightly reaching, by the end of 2020, almost 50% of the adult population in Brazil. From the income perspective, the use of credit reflects the country's inequality, as 50% of the population with the lowest income have approximately 12% of the credit portfolio balance in 2020. 

When analyzing the use of **digital financial services** , it was possible to look into a scenario of increasing digitalization. Even the lower income groups have increasingly sought relationships with IPs, which focus heavily on offering digital financial services. These groups also increasingly adopted Pix in the very first months after its implementation. The migration to digital occurs even in a scenario where income is configured as the main barrier for Brazilians to access the Internet and digital means of payment. 

The year 2020 could not be overlooked in the **analysis of recent developments** , a period strongly marked by the **impacts of the Covid-19 pandemic on financial citizenship** . Besides driving greater digitalization of financial services, the conditions imposed by the pandemic also had effects on other aspects of Brazilians' financial lives. The first effect was the expanded access, with an increase of almost 10% in the number of people in Brazil maintaining a relationship with the SFN, from 149 to 163 million in 2020. A relevant part of this expansion seems to be related to the Federal Emergency Aid, a benefit that may also be related to the more expressive drop in delinquencies specifically in that year.

##### **» Pix** 

###### **_#inclusion #access #use #quality_** 

Pix, the Brazilian instant payment arrangement, is the result of a working group in which several market agents have participated and that concluded its activities in December 2018 with the disclosure of the fundamental requirements for this ecosystem. In order to define its operating rules, the BCB established, in March 2019, the Pix Forum, a permanent advisory committee, with broad participation of market agents and public entities, which has been working on the continuous ecosystem’s improvement. Thus, on November 16, 2020, the BCB started the full operation of Pix.

Since its launch, Pix has turned in a new and effective alternative for the Brazilian population to make payments and transfers, alongside other means of payment such as cash, check, TED, DOC, slip, credit card, debit card, prepaid card, among others. Due to its characteristics (speed, availability, multiplicity of use, convenience, ease reconciliation for recipients, open environment, security, and low cost), Pix provides several benefits to its users and to the Brazilian economy, promoting competition, market efficiency, and financial inclusion.

The growth of new IPs accounts might have been associated to the search for remote access channels during the pandemic. This search also seems to have occurred by the low-income population who already maintained a relationship with financial institutions. Chapter 3 brings further details about IPs’ operations. The implementation of Pix has a great potential to boost digital financial inclusion In November 2020, BCB launched the Pix,37 with a potential to democratize the access to electronic payment services in the country and encourage even further the delivery of financial digital services to the lowincome population (see an analysis about the Pix in chapter 3). A few months after its implementation, data concerning the use of Pix by the low-income population already show the potential of change. In March 2021, 34.9% of the adult population in the _CadÚnico_ had already registered at least one Pix key, 21.4% had already sent a Pix transfer, and 24.6% had already received one (Figure 1.2.7). This figure shows data for the _Bolsa Família_ beneficiary groups and individuals registered in the _CadÚnico_ not benefited by the Program, as well as the remaining Brazilian adult population (not registered in the _CadÚnico_ ), for the sake of comparison. > 36 In Figure 1.2.6, “Other Segments” includes credit unions, specialized banks, credit institutions, and capital markets.

Compared with other electronic means of payment (Table 3.2.6), it is already possible to see a significant increase in the use of the Pix, as well as a drop in the number of other types of financial transactions.

Finally, **looking to the future** , the RCF highlighted **innovations** that have the potential to change the way financial services are offered. In this sense, it was observed that IPs have gained relevance in the financial lives of citizens, with their customer portfolio increasing from fifteen million in 2017 to sixty million in 2020. A second group of institutions with potential to impact financial citizenship, especially in the expansion of access to and use of credit, began operating in the SFN in this triennium were the SPEs and the SCDs, both known as credit fintechs. 

Besides the new institutions, specific innovations in the regulatory and payment environment brought important implications for financial citizenship: (i) **Open Banking** , which enables a scenario of greater competition, diversification and customization and tends to make services cheaper, more conveniently accessed by customers and better suited to the profile, needs and objectives of each person; (ii) the **Regulatory Sandbox** , which also fosters the creation of innovative products and services and has among its strategic priorities to encourage the emergence of financial and payment solutions with potential effects of stimulating financial inclusion and fostering credit for micro-entrepreneurs and small businesses; and (iii) the launch of **Pix** operation, which was conceived by BCB to facilitate the lives of citizens and companies, whether payers or payees. Pix seeks to enable new business models, reduce costs, contribute to the digitalization of means of payment and provide financial inclusion. 

The adoption of Pix, for example, was fast, and the **digitalization of means of payment with impacts on digital financial inclusion** also seems to have occurred on the very first months of operation. By August 2021, around forty million citizens who previously did not use electronic means of payment began to do so through Pix, which demonstrates effects beyond a simple change to other digital means of payment. 

These nuances in the analysis of **financial citizenship** show how this subject has advanced in recent years and highlight the various challenges yet to be overcome. The constant monitoring of this reality is essential for developing new technologies and innovative solutions and adequately evaluating their consequences on the lives of citizens and their relationship with the SFN.

###### Pix tomorrow 

Besides the major innovations introduced by Pix in its first months of operation, there are great expectations for the incorporation of other benefits to citizens, individual micro-entrepreneurs, individual entrepreneurs, and companies in general. The availability of new features and new Pix products is foreseen in the agenda for the coming years. 

Pix was developed by BCB to make life easier for individuals and companies, either as payers or as payees, and seeks to enable new business models, reduce costs, contribute to the digitalization of the means of payment, and provide the financial inclusion of the population. Its growing use,<sup>154</sup> encompassing increasingly types of use, has contributed to the construction of a more transparent, more competitive, more efficient, more inclusive, and more secure retail payments market, ultimately contributing to the financial citizenship. 

> 154 The continuous and fast expansion of Pix since its launch leads to the rapid change of statistics presented in this section over time. Further technical information about Pix is available at www.bcb.gov.br/pix.

Chapter 4 **_Conclusions_** 

Data and analyses in this Report show important advances in financial citizenship between 2018 and 2020. In 2018, the Financial Citizenship Report indicated in its conclusions that, as far as financial citizenship is concerned, future was heading to be digital. Great progress in this direction has been seen in recent years. The fast and growing adoption of Pix, the Brazilian instant payment scheme, is an example of digitalization with positive impacts on financial inclusion. 

In addition to highlighting the growing importance of digitalization, this Report has sought to broadly understand the transformations of financial citizenship. Based on three axes, the RCF aimed **to analyze the past, understand the main challenges of specific populations, and highlight the innovations in the SFN that will help shape the future of financial citizenship in Brazil.** 

In **analyzing the last three years** , the conclusion was that the scenario was one of preservation in terms of access to physical points of service for financial services. If, on the one hand, there was a drop in the number of branches, on the other hand there was an increase in the number of service points and banking correspondents.

**Instant Payment System (SPI)** : centralized and unique infrastructure managed by the BCB for the settlement of instant payments between distinct institutions in Brazil.  The system performs gross settlement in real time (RTGS), that is, it processes and settles transaction by transaction. Once settled, transactions are irrevocable. Instant payments are settled with entries in the special-purpose accounts – called Instant Payment Accounts (IP Accounts) – kept with the BCB by the institutions directly participating in the system. To ensure the soundness of the system, there is no possibility of overdraft entries, that is, PI Accounts do not allow for negative balance. 

**Pix transactions** : they comprise transactions settled in the SPI and information sent by Pix participants from transactions settled outside the SPI. Pix values and amounts are the sum of transactions performed in and out the SPI. 

**Average interest rate** : average of the interest rates on credit operations, weighted by the respective amounts disbursed. The average rates of the aggregate segments are calculated by the average rates of the credit types, weighted by the average balances of the respective types. Only operations agreed upon with prefixed rates are considered in this calculation. 

**Transfers** : in addition to Pix, transfers can be made by Credit Transfer Document (DOC) or Express Wire Transfer (TED). 

- **DOC** : interbank funds transfer order on behalf or in favor of individuals or legal entities, customers of financial institutions or payment institutions. It can only be sent and received by commercial banks, multiple banks with commercial portfolio, savings banks and payment institutions authorized to operate by the BCB. DOCs can only be issued in an amount up to BRL 4,999.99, and settlement occurs on the next business day following the date of issue. 

- **TED** : interbank funds transfer order, settled through a funds transfer settlement system, which is available to the receiving client within one hour and thirty minutes of the transfer execution. Account holders with the BCB – except for clearing houses and providers of clearing and settlement services – can offer TED to their clients, but there is no obligation. There is no minimum or maximum operational limit for sending funds through TED.

Credit operations abroad or operations which region is not informed were disregarded. **Instant Payment System (SPI)** : centralized and unique infrastructure managed by the BCB for the settlement of instant payments between distinct institutions in Brazil. The system performs gross settlement in real time (RTGS), that is, it processes and settles transaction by transaction. Once settled, transactions are irrevocable. Instant payments are settled with entries in the special-purpose accounts – called Instant Payment Accounts (IP Accounts) – kept with the BCB by the institutions directly participating in the system. To ensure the soundness of the system, there is no possibility of overdraft entries, that is, PI Accounts do not allow for negative balance. **Pix transactions** : they comprise transactions settled in the SPI and information sent by Pix participants from transactions settled outside the SPI. Pix values and amounts are the sum of transactions performed in and out the SPI. **Average interest rate** : average of the interest rates on credit operations, weighted by the respective amounts disbursed. The average rates of the aggregate segments are calculated by the average rates of the credit types, weighted by the average balances of the respective types. Only operations agreed upon with prefixed rates are considered in this calculation. **Transfers** : in addition to Pix, transfers can be made by Credit Transfer Document (DOC) or Express Wire Transfer (TED). - **DOC** : interbank funds transfer order on behalf or in favor of individuals or legal entities, customers of financial institutions or payment institutions. It can only be sent and received by commercial banks, multiple banks with commercial portfolio, savings banks and payment institutions authorized to operate by the BCB. DOCs can only be issued in an amount up to BRL 4,999.99, and settlement occurs on the next business day following the date of issue. - **TED** : interbank funds transfer order, settled through a funds transfer settlement system, which is available to the receiving client within one hour and thirty minutes of the transfer execution. Account holders with the BCB – except for clearing houses and providers of clearing and settlement services – can offer TED to their clients, but there is no obligation.
